Captured pre-M1 manifest.json — provenance
==========================================

file      pre-m1-manifest.json
sha256    1758a90253c220e579a1fd759644dc572694e9e01065beb6217135ec620e87a9
bytes     2875
revision  5c05a6d ("beads: split operator CLI core into bounded children"), the
          first parent of 53ae011 (PR #21) and so the last commit before manifest
          revision 1 sealed the zero-only escape ceiling.

These are the exact bytes that revision's OWN ceremony emitted, not a current set
edited to look old. The PROCEDURE below reproduces the shape, never these bytes:
that revision's `generate_node_identity` draws a random preimage and a random KDF
salt, so a second run of it emits a different manifest with a different checksum.

  git archive 5c05a6d | tar -x -C <scratch>
  # beside that revision's `ceremony_through_endorse`, add this test:
  #   let c = ceremony_through_endorse(3, 2); c.finalize().expect("finalize");
  #   std::fs::copy(c.dir.join("manifest.json"), <out>).expect("copy");
  cargo test -p vault-cli --bin btc-vault setup::tests::capture_pre_m1_manifest

The keys, endpoints and hashes are that throwaway ceremony's own; no live vault is
described here, and the manifest is never hash-authenticated under its own layout.
What matters is the shape: `protocol_version` is 0, `recovery_timelock` is present,
and the fields revisions 1 and 2 added — `escape_bump_max_fee_pct` and `network` —
are absent, which is why a syntax-tolerant parser must still read it.
